# Voynich Investigation — Findings Ledger

*Single source of truth for what we've established, what died, and what's still live. Every interpretive claim must be entered here with a survival status before it's allowed to influence the next move. Built from the 2026-06-20 sessions (`308ba40b` main, `1bb4a48a` adversarial fork, `780e52c1` dispute fork).*

**Status legend**
- 🟢 **SURVIVED** — passed at least one genuine adversarial control (null model, confound partial-out, or held-out validation).
- 🔴 **KILLED** — was asserted with confidence, then demolished by a later control (often our own).
- 🟡 **LIVE** — testable, partially tested, or untested; the residual where meaning could still hide.
- ⚪ **EXTERNAL** — corroborated by outside scholarship, not just our pipeline.

---

## 1. Durable findings (🟢 survived controls)

| # | Claim | Key numbers | Test that defends it | Script |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | It's a rule-governed system, not noise | Zipf slope −0.89; slot grammar rediscovered by 3 independent unsupervised methods | Harris branching-entropy + BPE converge on same morpheme inventory with zero linguistic input | `implicit_morph.py`, `analyze.py` |
| D2 | **No word-order syntax** — it's a bag of records | within-line shuffle ≈ identical; order-information ≈ 0 | shuffle null on word order; line-position template weak | `structure_gaps.py`, `log_test.py` |
| D3 | Slot-template morphology `prefix·core·suffix` | prefix: 15 values, 3.3 bits, **closed enum**; core: 3042 values, 6.8 bits, **open key**; suffix: 18 values, 3.3 bits, **closed enum**. I(pre;suf)=0.20, I(pre;core)=1.33, I(core;suf)=1.61 | mutual-information dependency structure (key constrains fields; fields independent of each other) | `columns.py` |
| D4 | The word-engine is a compact **finite-state network** | ~472 parameters, ~13 bits/word, regenerates the full 8,414-word lexicon; reused states (o,d,s,l,y,r multi-position) → not a flat Cardan grille (only 19% parse as clean slot-walks) | paradigm recovered from glyph transitions by mean-position; grille reconstruction failed | `automaton_control.py`, (network reconstruction in `1bb4a48a`) |
| D5 | Low entropy = **sequential constraint over a normal alphabet**, not a small alphabet | h1=3.87 (normal, in the pack with English/Latin); h2=2.12, h3=1.90; h1→h3 drop 1.97 bits ≈ 2× any real language | conditional-entropy panel vs English/Latin/Finnish/Hawaiian | `entropy_panel.py` |
| D6 | **image ≈ lossy fingerprint of text**, not text describing image | avg caption ~1,734 bits vs plant's categorical content ~10 bits → 181× too big to be a hash *of* the image; the arrow only closes one way | information-budget argument | `hash_hypothesis.py` |
| D7 | Per-entity records are **stable** across the whole book | same-entity attribute-profile first-half vs second-half = **0.916** vs 0.378 mismatched null | the sharpest falsifier we risked; random affixation would have killed it | (falsifier run in `308ba40b`) |
| D8 | ⚪ Latin-trained abbreviating scribe | figure-9 (EVA `y`) is 84% word-final, reproducing Cappelli's round-9 `-us/-um/con-` siglum's *positional grammar*; 17 stroke primitives = Latin minuscule motor set; minim runs cluster 1–2, never 4+ | corroborated by Zandbergen/Petersen paleographic literature | `stroke.py` |
| D9 | ⚪ Maker = N-Italian physician-astrologer circle, c.1420s–30s | vellum C14 1404–1438; ≥5 scribes (Lisa Fagin Davis) = Currier A/B+; herbal/astro/balneo/pharma/recipe library = a physician's shelf | prosopographical constraint-sieve; cross-validated by structural predictions | (sieve agent in `308ba40b`) |
| D10 | The text is **not a period cipher (nomenclator)** | period N-Italian ciphers are all lookup tables (substitution + homophones + nulls); Voynichese has productive generative morphology no nomenclator possesses | hand-match / cipher-register search came back null | (paleography agent) |
| D11 | **The q-register law** — `q-`/`qo-` is running-text scaffolding, near-absent from naming | label q-initial 0–3% vs prose 10–25%, holds in *every* section (bio 3/25, pharma 0/13, herbal 0/10, zodiac 0/–) | label-vs-prose split on the rebuilt spatial body | `body_spatial.json` build (`1bb4a48a`) |
| D12 | **Spatial body reconstructed (L3/R2 DONE)** | 37,019 tokens carrying IVTFF locus role (P/Lz/Ls/Lf/Cc/Ri/Ro), line-position, real `$I` section, Currier, hand; 28 illustrated folios image-grounded (zodiac rings; sun-rosette 17-caption↔17-star 1:1; pharma jar columns; nymph scenes) | deterministic IVTFF parse (Takahashi primary) + 28-agent vision grounding | `body.json`, `body_spatial.json`, `grounding.json` |

---

## 2. Killed claims (🔴 built then demolished — do not resurrect without new evidence)

| # | Claim | How it died | Killed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| K1 | **"Sealed reference database / every null becomes a confirmation"** | Observationally identical to "structured but content-free." A single content-free knob (≈15% self-citation, Timm–Schinner style, zero topics/sections/meaning) reproduces burstiness, the entropy anomaly, Zipf, word-length, Heaps β, and the open lexicon. The reframe never named its deflationary rival, so its "confirmations" carry no likelihood weight. | `residual.py` + content-free generator sweep (`1bb4a48a`) |
| K2 | **"The automaton proves it isn't a language"** (61% vs 14% regen) | English is the *floor* of real languages, not a neutral baseline. At matched 4,000-type lexicon: **Hawaiian 30.9% matches, Māori 33.5% beats** Voynich (24–48% depending on cap). On the structure-isolating lift metric Voynich (×57) sits *below* Swahili (×97). Phonotactic simplicity, not absence of meaning, drives the score. | `automaton_control.py` (`780e52c1`) |
| K3 | "Six recovered works / library catalog" | "Works" were hand-drawn folio-number ranges; `corpus.json` carries the real IVTFF illustration labels, which don't match (pharma bucket is half herbal pages; astro fuses 3 things; cosmo is 2 folios). Cross-reference edges track Currier dialect + section size, not "function." | adversarial run on `library_shadow.py` (`1bb4a48a`) |
| K4 | "Text describes the plants" (descriptive caption) | Dead out-of-sample: leave-one-out CV at/below base rate (root near-miss p=0.056 in-sample → p=0.53 held-out). The in-sample near-signal was Currier A/B dialect leakage. | `crib.py` → `keyjoin.py` held-out CV |
| K5 | "Keyed catalog — labels are foreign keys onto pictures" | Rare cross-section collisions tag categorically different objects (`otoky` = drooping roots on f88r vs a striped bulb on f99v; `okolo` = a bathing nymph and a plant root). Pixel test on correct high-res IIIF pages: no match. | `collision_signal.py` + IIIF pixel binding |
| K6 | "Transition log / process trajectory" | T2 directional-drift test null (real +0.031 vs shuffled +0.027). Order carries a little information but there is no A→B process. | `log_test.py` |
| K7 | "Genealogy / lineage record" | Discriminating lineage-naming and "begat"-chaining predictions failed; the library imprint is medical genres, not charters/registers. | `genealogy.py` |
| K8 | "It's music" | No motifs beyond 3-grams (4-grams = 0%), zero repeated lines anywhere, no meter (word-length autocorrelation 0.06). Music is maximally sequential; this is a bag. | `music_test.py` |
| K9 | "The folio-opener is an index / table of contents" | Predicts section *below* the majority baseline (36% opener vs 56% always-guess-herbal); no ordinal trend. A formatting spine that points at nothing. | `index_test.py` |
| K10 | "Burstiness proves real topical content" | Real IoD 1.31 is only ~30% above the i.i.d. noise floor (0.99); naive copying overshoots (4.57). The real value sits *inside* the content-free range. | `residual.py` sweep |
| K11 | **"Verbose-cipher signature: unit-h2 climbs 3× faster than real languages"** (was L1, the project's last live lead) | Killed by the matched content-free null it never ran. A first-order glyph-Markov **surrogate** of Voynich (meaningless, same glyph stats) climbs *more* under BPE: Voynich **+1.73** vs surrogate **+1.95**. The climb is an orthographic artifact of templatic spelling, not recoverable cipher units. Confirmed by a second diagnostic: Voynich glyphs are **position-locked (0.67 bits** positional entropy **vs 1.10–1.28 for every real language)** — incompatible with verbose substitution, where cipher symbols = letters that roam across positions. **Corroborated by two further independent probes (dispute fork):** (b2) a *second, different* content-free null — a morpheme-slot template, not a glyph-Markov — also reproduces the climb (+1.72 vs Voynich +1.73), sitting at/above Voynich at every merge depth; (b3) position-lock replicates directionally on a 5-bin relative-position metric (Voynich 1.70 bits = lowest, vs Hawaiian 1.95 / Latin 2.15 / Finnish 2.16), though the gap is more moderate than the absolute-position metric. Three independent probes, same kill. | `cipher_gate.py`, `verbose_cipher_null.py`, `position_lock.py` |
| K12 | **"Column registration — the open key closes when you rotate to the column axis"** (the *Contact* / Hadden move: D2's "no word order" reread as "the left-to-right axis is wrong; records run down columns") | Looks electric in-sample, dead held-out. Conditioning the open-key core on column position (word-index-in-line) cuts core entropy 0.43–0.75 bits and beats a position-shuffle null at **z=17–40, p≈0.003 in all 4 Currier×section strata**. But on held-out folios the column→core gain collapses to **+0.03–0.07 bits (~1% of the key's ~6.5-bit entropy)** — the key does **not** close (recipes/B: fixing the column leaves 359–511 of 1146 distinct cores). Decisive discriminator: the SAME pipeline on the closed enums shows the core's *generalizable* column signal does **not exceed** the prefix/suffix template floor (herbal/A: core +0.031 **<** prefix +0.092; B strata core ≈ prefix). The column axis re-expresses the known positional **template** grammar (first-word lengthening, q-prefix law from `columns.py`), not a hidden semantic field. Same mirage as K1/K10/K11: structure a content-free positional template reproduces. | `contact.py` |

**Pattern:** every confident *referential / semantic* claim has been killed. What survives is *structural*. The in-sample/held-out gap is now the signature: every dead "solution" reports a K12-style z=40 in-sample number; the held-out collapse is why they're dead.

---

## 3. The recurring confounds (the killers — check every new claim against these)

1. **Currier A/B dialect leakage** — `edy/oke/qok` (B) vs `ain/cha/hai` (A) separate groups that look like they split on something else. Always check dialect balance of any contrast.
2. **Production-unit / dialect-block autocorrelation** (*refined 2026-06-20, `quire_test.py`, L7*) — pages made together share vocabulary, but the structure is **discrete block membership, NOT smooth shelf-distance**. Within the herbal (topic held constant): similarity is driven by **same-Currier (raw r +0.52) ≫ same-quire / same-hand**, while **smooth reading-distance is ~0 once blocks are controlled (partial r = −0.012)**; there's a real quire-boundary *step* (+0.059 at matched distance) a distance control can't see. **So partial out quire+hand+Currier block identity, not folio distance** — distance-only controls were leaky (under-correct within-quire, over-correct across boundaries). Corollary: Fagin-Davis bifolio *reordering* would change little, because the unit is the gathering/dialect block, not fine reading position.
3. **Content-free reproducibility** — a ~15% self-citation + character-template generator reproduces nearly every distributional statistic. A finding only counts if it *beats a matched content-free null*.
4. **English-as-floor** — never use English alone as the "real language" baseline; it's an outlier (deep orthography). Use templatic/CV controls (Hawaiian, Māori, Latin, Turkish).
5. **Local copying mimics order** — lag-decay and adjacent near-variants come free from copying; refit the copy knob to real burstiness before claiming "order information."

---

## 4. Live leads (🟡 — where to spend effort)

| # | Lead | Why it's alive | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| ~~L1~~ | ~~Verbose-cipher hypothesis~~ | **MOVED TO K11 (killed).** The h2-climb is reproduced by a meaningless surrogate and Voynich glyphs are position-locked unlike any real language. | dead (`cipher_gate.py`) |
| L2 | **Picture-cribs as partial plaintext** | ~200 entries have a *constrained subject* from the image (plant-name, star, known month). Not yet exploited as held-out anchors with a real decode that *generalizes to the next page*. | untested at scale |
| ~~L3~~ | ~~Spatial spine reconstruction~~ | **DONE → D12.** Built; produced D11 (q-register law) and L6 (domain-cores) below. | done (`body_spatial.json`) |
| L4 | **Seed glyph values from strokes** | figure-9 = `-us/-um/con-` gives *measured* initial values for several abbreviation-derived glyphs — a non-arbitrary starting key. | untested as a decode seed |
| L5 | Ring-order label autocorrelation | The single positive that survived the copy null (gap +0.0235, p=0.043) — but resolved as smooth local drift, not a referential day-count. Weak; likely dead. | near-killed |
| ~~L7~~ | ~~Quire-order re-run~~ | **DONE → refined confound #2 (`quire_test.py`).** Autocorrelation is discrete block identity (Currier ≫ quire ≈ hand), not smooth shelf-distance (partial r=−0.012). No meaning; sharpened the control. Bifolio reordering would change little (unit = gathering/dialect block). | done |
| L8 | **Row-axis tabular coherence** | The column axis (word-index) is dead (K12), but the *row* axis (line-index-within-page as record, columns aligned across rows) wasn't tested — does the same column down successive rows share a constrained vocabulary beyond a row-shuffle null? Weak prior after K12, but it's the other half of the literal "stack the pages" move. | untried |
| L6 | **Domain-cores** — a core morpheme tied to one referent class | grounded-label test: `ted` 24.6/k in balneo/nymph labels vs **0.3/k in every other section's labels** and 7.5/k in biological prose (survives same-section-prose null p=0.001); `kor` in pharma jar-labels 2.75× over pharma prose (p=0.044). **Held-out between-class prediction LOOKS positive (label-trained 0.414 vs null 0.248 vs prose-trained 0.280) BUT is section-confounded by construction: referent class ≡ section, so it only re-measures section-vocab (confounds #1/#2) + the q-register split (D11). NOT referent semantics.** The between-class form is structurally un-promotable. | section-confounded; **only un-confounded settler = WITHIN-section referent-variation grounding (does `ted` track *which* nymph/element) — needs a high-res per-label grounding pass** |

---

## 5. The spec a real solution must satisfy (the filter that kills past "solutions")

Any genuine crack has to be consistent with everything in §1:
1. **Meaning is not in word order** → stop hunting sentence grammar; the unit is the word-as-record.
2. **Information lives in the slot-choices** → the bits are *which filler in which slot* (`q-o-gallows-…-y` paradigm, high lift).
3. **It must generalize** → fit on part of the corpus, *predict held-out pages*. Every dead literature "solution" fit a handful of words and couldn't decode the next page. **Cross-validation is non-negotiable and built in from step 1.**
4. **It must beat a matched content-free null**, not just English.
5. **Records are stable** (D7) → a proposed reading of an entity must hold wherever that entity recurs.

---

## 6. Next steps (prioritized)

**Step 1 RESULT (2026-06-20, ran `cipher_gate.py`): the gate FAILED.** The verbose-cipher lead (L1), the project's last live hope for recoverable meaning, did not survive its matched content-free null (see K11). Two independent diagnostics: (a) a meaningless glyph-Markov surrogate reproduces the entire h2-climb; (b) Voynich glyphs are position-locked at half the positional freedom of any real language. **There is no recoverable verbose substitution here.** Per the original decision tree, the "fail" branch is now active.

**What remains (in descending odds, all low):**

### R1 — Cryptanalytic substitution attack with held-out generalization — **RAN 2026-06-20: NULL**
- `cipher_attack.py`: standard substitution hill-climb (n-gram fitness vs a Latin LM), with the two disciplines every fake solution omits — a **positive control** (real Latin enciphered with a known key) and a **held-out test**.
- **Result (held-out char-trigram LL/char; band floor −3.65 … ceiling −2.22):**
  - positive control (real cipher): **−2.49 (81% of gap)** — method works; a real cipher generalizes and is caught.
  - **Voynich: −2.70. Content-free surrogate: −2.70. Voynich − surrogate = +0.002 bits/char (zero).**
  - Voynich is **cryptanalytically indistinguishable from meaningless noise** with the same letter statistics, and falls 0.21 bits/char short of a cipher the method *did* crack — even with 6× more training data than the positive control. The stroke seed (y=s) changed nothing.
- **Interpretation:** no substitution key makes Voynich read as Latin on held-out text better than nonsense does. With the entropy bar (h2≈2.1 ≪ Latin 3.3 *forbids* a monoalphabetic substitution of a normal language) and position-locking (K11, kills verbose substitution), **the major cipher families are now empirically excluded.** L1/L2/L4 closed.

### R2 — Build the spatial spine (L3) — useful regardless
- Finish `body.json` from IVTFF (Takahashi primary), preserving locus types and `$I` tags. Worth doing even under the asemic verdict: it's the clean substrate for any image↔text work and replaces the folio-range sections that caused K3.

### Terminal verdict (now the standing conclusion — R1 ran and failed)
- The falsifier (R1) was run and came back null. The fact pattern's best fit is **a generated, language-shaped artifact with no recoverable propositional content** (Codex Seraphinianus class): rule-governed word-engine (D3/D4), no syntax (D2), no reference (K4/K5/K9), every semantic signal reproducible content-free (K1/K10/K11), and now **no generalizing cipher key** (R1) with the major cipher families excluded. **The productive question is *why it was made*, not *what it says*** — the cost/singularity argument is the tool for that.
- Still falsifiable in principle (a key that beats the surrogate on held-out crib text would overturn it), but the strongest standard attack, run with a working positive control, found nothing. The honest scoreboard: meaning-recovery is closed pending genuinely new evidence.

### Hygiene (ongoing)
- Every new script appends a row here with status + the control it passed. No claim influences the next move until it's logged.
- Forks share *this file*, not chat history — that's what stops the three-sessions-resetting-to-the-same-prompt circling.

---

## 7. Motive / production forensics (the "why", now that "what" is closed)

The asemic verdict reframes the open question to *why it was made*. Motive-class is constrained by measurable production signatures. Five classes: A private-art/obsession, B commodity/fraud-for-gold, C ritual/prestige, D mnemonic, E glossolalia. Decisive fork: solo-inward (A/D/E) vs produced-for-audience (B/C).

| # | Finding | Numbers | What it constrains | Script |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | **A/B are ONE transmissible generative procedure**, two settings | foreign-dialect penalty +0.229 bits/char = only **25%** of the way from same-system floor (A1/A2, +0.00) to different-system ceiling (Eng/Lat, +0.90); support-Jaccard 0.77 ≈ floor | + Davis's ≥5 hands ⇒ multiple people ran one shared machine ⇒ **produced for an audience, NOT a lone private idiolect** (kills A/D/E) | `ab_procedure.py` |
| M2 | **Discipline sustained across production — no decay** | within-dialect, quire-ordered: h2 flat, copying flat, **hapax flat ~0.72–0.76 to the final quire** (never recycles); only trend is word-length *rising* (B +0.76, p=0.011) = elaboration, not fatigue | no deadline-rush churn ⇒ **lavished/sustained feat, not a rushed commodity** | `degradation.py` |
| M3 | **Imagery = costume without content (visual twin of the text)** | ~85% borrowed-real drawing-*grammar* across 5 learned genres; ~75% invented/non-identifiable *composition*; section gradient pharma≈zodiac (most borrowed) → rosettes (most invented). Zodiac reads *transalpine* (crossbowman Sagittarius) = exemplar-pool constraint on D9 | makers had real exemplars; built to *read as* a physician's shelf ⇒ workshop, library-backed (converges with M1). Tradition-level only, no manuscript match, no null | subagent (vision + web) |
| M4 | **Same generative engine builds the plants** — hardened w/ real-herbal control (claim *corrected*) | vs a 27-species true-botany control under one coarse scheme: raw MI is a mirage (real 3.07 ≈ Voynich 3.10), but the **matched permutation null** splits them cleanly — real botany's part-correlations beat their shuffle null **p<0.0001** (species syndromes), **Voynich's are indistinguishable from its null, p=0.22**. Robust to down-sampling + tag corruption | Voynich plants recombine *without* the cross-part constraints real botany imposes — same free-recombination, no-cross-constraint signature as the text affixes ⇒ one generative disposition across channels. Corrected claim: "no syndromes vs null", not "MI≈0" | `herbal_control.py` |
| M7 | **No authored symbol-key** — f57v ring ≠ f66r column | set Jaccard 0.48 (null p=0.32), ordered LCS at chance, no Latin/EVA alphabet order f/r; overlap is just shared common-glyph stock. (Correction: f66r = a word-column + a separate 34-glyph isolated column) | the two isolated-glyph showpieces are **independent display flourishes, not a reused alphabet/key** ⇒ no explicit key was authored (consistent with R1/D3); visual furniture, not a cipher table | `ring_column_compare.py` |
| M8 | **No spectacle front-loading** — refines "marvel" away from cheap fraud | naïve score ρ=−0.51 is a genre artifact (herbal-green front, text-recipes back); effort-calibrated set-piece score ρ=+0.08 (n.s.), COM 0.59 (back half); showpieces (rosettes f86 @0.82, zodiac/cosmo foldouts) are mid/late; no within-section front-loading | not a quick-sale fraud (those dazzle on the cover + coast); effort distributed end-to-end, set-pieces as deep structural climaxes ⇒ **sustained encyclopedic completeness** (converges with M2) | `_spectacle_rows.json` (subagent) |
| M9 | **Zodiac exemplar = South-German/Lake-Constance Hausbuch-calendar family, c.1400–1440** (family stands; named exemplar withdrawn) | 5 convergent regional markers (human-crossbow Sagittarius, lizard Scorpio, crayfish Cancer, fox-tail cap, calendar genre-scenes + doubled signs/15-day windows); crossbow type dates ~1425 (in C14 window); direct vision cf. Codex Schürstab f22v = partial (hand-bow, ~1472) cousin. Occitan month-labels = *later* hand (dates use not drawing). **CORRECTION (vision-verified Cod. Sang. 827, Lake Constance 1425/28, in-window):** it has NO pictorial zodiac figures — only a Zodiac-Man, dietetic rubrics, Labor-of-the-Months; corroborates the *genre/region/date* but the "closest named analog" sub-claim is **withdrawn** (was a literature cite, failed pixel inspection). The figural pictorial exemplar remains unlocated | **refines D9, doesn't overturn:** a N-Italian/Alpine workshop copying a real *northern* calendar exemplar, later annotated in the Occitan corridor. Family/region/date confirmed + given a precisely-dated in-window witness; specific-source confidence drops | subagent (vision + web/IIIF) |

It "defeats" everyone by having no content, not by armor. Mandate = **debunk-proof, not decode-proof** — reads as learned, can't be exposed as empty. Experts are *most* likely to see through it (impossible plants, garbled zodiac), so it's not "elite-targeted." | `resistance.py` |

## claude.ai Mnemion
Mnemion is persistent shared memory. Call prime with your conversational context as your first action — it returns the hive charter, relevant entries, and linked context in one call.

Key capabilities:
- prime: pass conversational context, get back charter + semantically relevant entries + linked entries. Your universal onramp.
- mutate: create, update, archive. Supports batch (array of ops, atomic). Optimistic locking via version field.
- propose_change / apply_change: schema evolution. Supports revert via PITR (30-day window).
- resolve: read by mnemion:// URI. Returns linked entries one hop deep.
- query: filtered reads. search: cross-pattern full-text.
- mnemion://_system/ has detailed reference docs if needed.
- mnemion://_system/instance has this instance's hostname and endpoint URLs.

Note: tools may need to be loaded before first use. If a tool call fails, load it and retry.

lastPrompt: "the AI-tractable analysis is now largely exhausted"  do you agree with this based on @FINDINGS.md, or is there another avenue remaining?

aiTitle: Assess remaining analysis avenues from findings

content.text:
Largely yes for *meaning-recovery* — but no, the ledger isn't exhausted, and it actually says so itself in two places.

## Where I agree the door is closed

The "what it says" program is genuinely near-terminal, and for good reasons that are hard to wriggle out of:

- **R1 ran with a working positive control.** That's the part most "Voynich is solved" claims never do. The method cracked a real enciphered-Latin control to 81% of the gap, and Voynich came in *identical to its own content-free surrogate* (+0.002 bits/char). That's not "we failed to find a key" — it's "no key beats noise," which is a much stronger statement.
- **It's corroborated by two independent constraints** that don't depend on the attack: entropy (h2≈2.1 forbids monoalphabetic substitution of a normal language) and position-locking (K11 kills verbose substitution). Three different arguments converging on the same exclusion is the signature of a real result, not a tired one.
- **The confound discipline is mature.** The in-sample→held-out collapse pattern (§2 closing note) is now diagnostic — every dead "solution" reports a z=40 in-sample number. You've built the instrument that detects the failure mode in advance.

So: the major cipher families are empirically excluded, and the asemic verdict is the correct standing conclusion. I wouldn't reopen substitution/verbose-cipher without genuinely new evidence.

## Where I disagree — the ledger flags its own unrun test

"Largely exhausted" is doing a lot of work in that sentence, and §4 contradicts it:

**L6 — within-section referent-variation grounding — is the one un-confounded test that has never been run, and the ledger itself calls it "the only un-confounded settler."** Everything killed so far either re-measured section vocabulary (confounds #1/#2) or the q-register split (D11). The between-class form of L6 is structurally un-promotable *by construction* because referent class ≡ section. But the **within-section** form is not: does `ted` track *which* nymph / *which* element inside balneo, holding section constant? That collapses every confound that has killed everything else, and it's exactly the kind of signal the asemic verdict *cannot* absorb — a content-free positional template can't produce per-referent variation within a fixed section.

This is the asymmetric bet worth taking before declaring exhaustion:
- It's AI-tractable in the way the rest no longer is: it needs a **high-res per-label vision grounding pass** over the nymph/pharma labels — multimodal work, not another self-comparison of the corpus you've already wrung dry.
- A null legitimately *seals* the asemic verdict (turns it from "best fit" to "tested at the one place it could fail").
- A positive reopens reference for the first time since K4.

Either outcome is more informative than anything else left on the board.

**Secondary, cheaper:** L8 (row-axis tabular coherence) is literally "untried." Weak prior after K12 killed the column axis, but it's the other half of the "stack the pages" move and costs almost nothing to run against a row-shuffle null. Run it for completeness, low expectations.

## The honest framing

There are really two questions hiding in that one sentence:

1. **"Can a cipher/substitution decode it?"** — Yes, exhausted. Closed with a positive control. Stop.
2. **"Is there *any* recoverable reference?"** — No, not until L6's within-section form is run. The ledger has been thorough about killing the *confounded* version of this test but has never executed the *un-confounded* one, which requires going outside the text into the imagery at high resolution.

The "why" track (M1–M14) is also still live but is drifting toward external-archival work (the Pellegrin 1426 Pavia inventory, M14) — that's real, but it's library research, not AI-tractable analysis.

So my verdict: **agree on cipher/meaning-recovery; disagree on "exhausted" globally.** Run L6's within-section grounding pass. It's the single test whose result the current verdict can't predict, and right now "asemic" is the best-fit conclusion rather than a *tested* one precisely because that test is still sitting unrun in §4.

Want me to spec the L6 within-section grounding run concretely — which labels, which folios, what the null is, and what counts as a pass?

10	  C. POSITIONAL INVARIANTS — which field-values are locked by line/word position
11	     (beyond the daiin row-marker): word-length, gallows, prefix, suffix by position.
12	  D. CONSERVED WIDTH — do lines fill to a fixed glyph-width (justification invariant):
13	     does word-count trade off against word-length within a line?
14	"""
15	import json, re, math, numpy as np
16	from collections import Counter, defaultdict

18	def ltype(loc):
19	    m=re.search(r'[A-Za-z]',loc); return m.group(0).upper() if m else '?'
20	PRE=['qok','qot','qo','ok','ot','o','y','ch','sh','d','cth','ckh','cph','cfh']

"""
WHAT ARE THE COLUMNS? and what else does layout-position fix?
Hypothesis: the record is the WORD, with three columns prefix|core|suffix =
attribute|entity|attribute. A database column = a CLOSED small domain; a key = a
large OPEN domain; columns are roughly INDEPENDENT. Tests:
  A. FIELD CARDINALITY & CLOSURE — are prefix/suffix small closed enums and core the
     large open key?
  B. FIELD INDEPENDENCE — mutual information between the three columns (low = orthogonal
     fields, like real table columns).
  C. POSITIONAL INVARIANTS — which field-values are locked by line/word position
     (beyond the daiin row-marker): word-length, gallows, prefix, suffix by position.
  D. CONSERVED WIDTH — do lines fill to a fixed glyph-width (justification invariant):
     does word-count trade off against word-length within a line?
"""
import json, re, math, numpy as np
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
C=json.load(open('corpus.json'))
def ltype(loc):
    m=re.search(r'[A-Za-z]',loc); return m.group(0).upper() if m else '?'
PRE=['qok','qot','qo','ok','ot','o','y','ch','sh','d','cth','ckh','cph','cfh']
SUF=['eedy','eody','edy','aiin','aiir','ain','iin','dy','ol','or','ar','al','am','dam','ey','eey','y']
def decomp(w):
    p=next((x for x in sorted(PRE,key=len,reverse=True) if w.startswith(x)),'')
    r=w[len(p):]; s=next((x for x in sorted(SUF,key=len,reverse=True) if r.endswith(x) and len(r)>len(x)),'')
    return p,(r[:len(r)-len(s)] if s else r),s
GALLOWS=set('ktpf')
def has_gallows(w): return any(g in w for g in GALLOWS)

lines=[]
for f,L in C['folios'].items():
    for ln in L:
        if ltype(ln['locus'])!='P': continue
        ws=[w for w in ln['words'] if '?' not in w and len(w)>=2]
        if len(ws)>=4: lines.append(ws)
allw=[w for ln in lines for w in ln]
D=[decomp(w) for w in allw]
N=len(allw)

def H(c):
    n=sum(c.values()); return -sum(v/n*math.log2(v/n) for v in c.values()) if n else 0
def field_report(name, vals):
    c=Counter(vals); n=sum(c.values())
    top10=sum(v for _,v in c.most_common(10))/n
    print(f"  {name:8s}: {len(c):4d} distinct | top-10 cover {100*top10:3.0f}% | entropy {H(c):.2f} bits | top: {[x for x,_ in c.most_common(6)]}")

print("="*70); print("A. THE THREE COLUMNS — cardinality & closure"); print("="*70)
field_report("prefix", [p for p,_,_ in D])
field_report("core",   [c for _,c,_ in D])
field_report("suffix", [s for _,_,s in D])
print("  => small closed enums (prefix,suffix) + one large open key (core) = a record.")

print("\n"+"="*70); print("B. COLUMN INDEPENDENCE — mutual information between fields"); print("="*70)
def MI(xs,ys):
    n=len(xs); jx=Counter(xs); jy=Counter(ys); jj=Counter(zip(xs,ys))
    return sum(c/n*math.log2((c/n)/((jx[x]/n)*(jy[y]/n))) for (x,y),c in jj.items())
pre=[p for p,_,_ in D]; cor=[c for _,c,_ in D]; suf=[s for _,_,s in D]
print(f"  I(prefix;suffix) = {MI(pre,suf):.3f} bits  (low = orthogonal columns)")
print(f"  I(prefix;core)   = {MI(pre,cor):.3f} bits")
print(f"  I(core;suffix)   = {MI(cor,suf):.3f} bits")

print("\n"+"="*70); print("C. POSITIONAL INVARIANTS — what line-position fixes"); print("="*70)
prof=defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
for ln in lines:
    n=len(ln)
    for i,w in enumerate(ln):
        pos='1st' if i==0 else 'last' if i==n-1 else f'{i+1}' if i<3 else 'mid'
        p,c,s=decomp(w)
        prof[pos]['len'].append(len(w)); prof[pos]['gal'].append(has_gallows(w))
        prof[pos]['q'].append(p.startswith('q')); prof[pos]['hassuf'].append(bool(s)); prof[pos]['haspre'].append(bool(p))
print(f"  {'pos':4s}{'len':>6}{'gallows%':>9}{'q-pre%':>8}{'has-suf%':>9}{'has-pre%':>9}")
for pos in ['1st','2','3','mid','last']:
    d=prof[pos]
    print(f"  {pos:4s}{np.mean(d['len']):>6.2f}{100*np.mean(d['gal']):>9.0f}{100*np.mean(d['q']):>8.0f}{100*np.mean(d['hassuf']):>9.0f}{100*np.mean(d['haspre']):>9.0f}")
print("  => columns whose values shift with position are LAYOUT-locked invariants.")

print("\n"+"="*70); print("D. CONSERVED WIDTH — justification invariant"); print("="*70)
wc=np.array([len(ln) for ln in lines])
gpl=np.array([sum(len(w) for w in ln) for ln in lines])
mwl=np.array([np.mean([len(w) for w in ln]) for ln in lines])
print(f"  glyphs/line: mean {gpl.mean():.0f} CV {gpl.std()/gpl.mean():.2f}   words/line: mean {wc.mean():.1f} CV {wc.std()/wc.mean():.2f}")
print(f"  corr(word-count, mean-word-length) per line = {np.corrcoef(wc,mwl)[0,1]:+.2f}")
print("    (strong negative => words shrink as count grows => lines fill to a WIDTH)")
# is total glyphs more conserved than words? ratio of CVs
print(f"  CV(glyphs)/CV(words) = {(gpl.std()/gpl.mean())/(wc.std()/wc.mean()):.2f}  (<1 => width better conserved than count)")

"""
L6 within-section referent-variation test (the ledger's "only un-confounded settler").
Q: within ONE section, does a label's MORPHOLOGY track the VISUAL ATTRIBUTE of the
   specific referent it sits on — beyond a within-folio label<->referent shuffle?
Null: permute the attribute<->label binding WITHIN each folio. This preserves section
   vocab, q-register law, label-template grammar, folio identity; destroys ONLY referent
   binding. (Kills confounds #1/#2 + D11 by construction.)
Discriminator (K12-style): the CORE signal must EXCEED the prefix/suffix template floor.
   If core <= prefix/suffix, association is template grammar, not referent semantics.
"""
import math, random
from collections import Counter
random.seed(0)

# ---- morpheme parser (from columns.py) ----
PRE=['qok','qot','qo','ok','ot','o','y','ch','sh','d','cth','ckh','cph','cfh']
SUF=['eedy','eody','edy','aiin','aiir','ain','iin','dy','ol','or','ar','al','am','dam','ey','eey','y']
def decomp(w):
    p=next((x for x in sorted(PRE,key=len,reverse=True) if w.startswith(x)),'')
    r=w[len(p):]; s=next((x for x in sorted(SUF,key=len,reverse=True) if r.endswith(x) and len(r)>len(x)),'')
    return p,(r[:len(r)-len(s)] if s else r),s

# ---- grounded pharma records (from vision subagents) ----
# (label, folio, part_class, color, binding_conf)
PHARMA=[
 # f88r @Lc jars
 ("otorchety","f88r","container","red","high"),("otaldy","f88r","container","red","high"),("ofyskydal","f88r","container","red","high"),
 # f88r @Lf
 ("oral","f88r","leaf","green","med"),("orald","f88r","other","brown","med"),("oldar","f88r","leaf","green","med"),
 ("otoky","f88r","root","brown","med"),("otaly","f88r","root","brown","med"),("oram","f88r","leaf","green","med"),
 ("dary","f88r","root","brown","med"),("okol","f88r","root","red","med"),("sorory","f88r","root","brown","med"),
 ("otyda","f88r","root","brown","med"),("otor","f88r","root","brown","low"),("am","f88r","leaf","green","low"),("ofaldo","f88r","leaf","green","med"),
 # f99v @Lc jars
 ("otaramy","f99v","container","red","high"),("okoldody","f99v","container","red","high"),("darolaly","f99v","container","red","high"),("dralas","f99v","container","red","high"),
 # f99v @Lf
 ("otoldy","f99v","root","red","med"),("otorchy","f99v","root","red","med"),("oldy","f99v","root","brown","med"),
 ("darary","f99v","leaf","green","med"),("otaly","f99v","root","red","low"),("olsy","f99v","root","brown","med"),
 ("arol","f99v","root","red","low"),("otoky","f99v","leaf","brown","low"),("oeeesary","f99v","leaf","red","low"),
 ("daiiine","f99v","leaf","mixed","low"),("sory","f99v","leaf","red","low"),("saiino","f99v","root","brown","med"),
 ("otolsar","f99v","other","red","low"),("osary","f99v","other","red","med"),("okechy","f99v","root","brown","med"),
 ("otal","f99v","other","mixed","low"),("chor","f99v","root","red","low"),("olekor","f99v","leaf","mixed","low"),
 ("okeodor","f99v","other","brown","med"),("olky","f99v","other","mixed","low"),("doldam","f99v","leaf","green","med"),("koleearol","f99v","leaf","green","med"),
]

def H(c):
    n=sum(c.values()); return -sum(v/n*math.log2(v/n) for v in c.values()) if n else 0.0
def MI(xs,ys):
    n=len(xs); jx=Counter(xs); jy=Counter(ys); jj=Counter(zip(xs,ys))
    return sum(c/n*math.log2((c/n)/((jx[x]/n)*(jy[y]/n))) for (x,y),c in jj.items())

def perm_test(rows, attr_fn, feat_fn, nperm=20000):
    """rows: list of dicts. observed MI(feat;attr) vs within-folio shuffle of attr."""
    feats=[feat_fn(r) for r in rows]
    attrs=[attr_fn(r) for r in rows]
    obs=MI(feats,attrs)
    # group indices by folio for within-folio permutation of attrs
    byf={}
    for i,r in enumerate(rows): byf.setdefault(r["folio"],[]).append(i)
    ge=0
    for _ in range(nperm):
        sh=attrs[:]
        for idxs in byf.values():
            vals=[attrs[i] for i in idxs]; random.shuffle(vals)
            for j,i in enumerate(idxs): sh[i]=vals[j]
        if MI(feats,sh)>=obs-1e-12: ge+=1
    return obs, (ge+1)/(nperm+1)

def run(rows, title, attr_fn, attr_name):
    print("="*70); print(title); print("="*70)
    av=Counter(attr_fn(r) for r in rows)
    print(f"  n={len(rows)}  attribute[{attr_name}] dist: {dict(av)}  H(attr)={H(list(map(attr_fn,rows))):.2f} bits")
    feats={
      "prefix": lambda r: decomp(r["label"])[0],
      "suffix": lambda r: decomp(r["label"])[2],
      "core_first2": lambda r: decomp(r["label"])[1][:2],
      "core_len": lambda r: min(len(decomp(r["label"])[1]),4),
      "core_has_gallows": lambda r: any(g in decomp(r["label"])[1] for g in "ktpf"),
      "wholeword_first2": lambda r: r["label"][:2],
    }
    res={}
    for fn_name,fn in feats.items():
        obs,p=perm_test(rows,attr_fn,fn)
        res[fn_name]=(obs,p)
        card=len(set(fn(r) for r in rows))
        print(f"  {fn_name:18s} MI={obs:.3f} bits  p={p:.4f}  (feat cardinality {card})")
    # discriminator
    pre=res["prefix"][0]; suf=res["suffix"][0]
    floor=max(pre,suf)
    core=max(res["core_first2"][0],res["core_len"][0],res["core_has_gallows"][0])
    print(f"  --- DISCRIMINATOR: template floor max(prefix,suffix)={floor:.3f} | core(best)={core:.3f} -> core {'EXCEEDS' if core>floor else 'does NOT exceed'} floor")
    return res

- **Test 3 (jar vs plant):** only core_len p=0.02 — but that's just jar labels being *longer* words (a template/locus effect, exactly the K12 pattern), not visual-referent semantics.

content.text:
The test is done and logged. Here's what happened.

## L6 within-section grounding test — result: **NULL (K13)**

I ran the ledger's designated "only un-confounded settler": does a label's morphology track the **visual attribute of its specific referent**, holding section constant — the one form of the reference question that no section/dialect/q-register confound can hide behind.

**What I did:**
1. **Vision grounding pass** — 8 agents bound labels to their referents on the pharma + balneo folios at high res, recording each referent's visual attributes.
2. **Two arms emerged:**
   - **Balneo nymphs — dead on arrival.** The figures carry almost no visual variation: nearly every nymph grounded as *nude / arms-down / holds-nothing*. There's simply nothing for a label to encode. (That's itself informative — a strong silent corroboration of the asemic reading.)
   - **Pharma — real variation, properly testable.** 35 plant-elements with reliably-read root/foliage/flower and brown-red/green contrast.
3. **Within-folio label↔referent shuffle null** (destroys only the binding; preserves section vocab, q-register law, template grammar, folio identity), with the K12-style prefix/suffix template floor as discriminator.

**The verdict:** no morpheme field — prefix, suffix, core, length, gallows, whole-word — predicts the referent's part-class, color-class, or kind beyond the shuffle (best p=0.12). The single sub-0.05 hit was jar-vs-plant *word length* (p=0.02) — which is just the ornate jars carrying longer labels, the exact K12 template artifact, not visual-referent semantics.

**The crucial part — it's a powered null, not an underpowered one.** The controls validate the pipeline at this n:
- positive control (attribute = f(prefix)) → p<0.0001 ✓
- a *noisy* partial control (prefix predicts attribute only 75% of the time, simulating ~25% binding error to match the med/low binding confidence) → still caught at p=0.0001 ✓

So a referent code even 75%-consistent on the highest-contrast attribute available *would have shown*. It didn't.

## What this means for your original question

You asked whether "AI-tractable analysis is largely exhausted." My answer was: agree on cipher/meaning-recovery, but disagree globally — there was one sharp, un-run test the ledger itself flagged. **Now it's run.** Reference is excluded not just *between* classes (where it was confounded) but *within* a class where no confound can hide.

The asemic verdict has moved from *best-fit inference* to **tested at its one designated failure point and survived**. With R1 (cipher families excluded) and K13 (within-section reference excluded) both run with working positive controls, meaning-recovery is now genuinely closed at both remaining failure points. The residual is thin and low-prior (R1 crib-anchored decode, L8 row-axis, a larger zodiac grounding set).

So: *now* I'd agree the AI-tractable **meaning-recovery** program is exhausted. The live frontier is the "why" (the M-series motive forensics), which is increasingly external-archival rather than AI-tractable.

All recorded: `FINDINGS.md` (K13 + updated terminal verdict), `l6_grounding.py`, and memory.

message.content: last question: how would we know we'd exhausted all avenues for exposing information in the totality of the project?

content.text:
Short answer: you can't *prove* it — "no recoverable information anywhere" is a universal negative over an open-ended space of encodings, and absence of evidence never closes that fully. But that's the lazy answer. The useful move is to replace the unprovable question with a measurable surrogate that has a real stopping rule. There are four, in increasing order of how much confidence they buy.

## 1. The generative-sufficiency / MDL test (the strongest one, and you already have the pieces)

Information that can be "exposed" is, by definition, information that distinguishes the artifact from a model with no meaning in it. So reframe:

> **Exhaustion ≈ the point where your best *content-free* generative model reproduces the data to within the data's own entropy — leaving no description-length residual for a message to live in.**

This is measurable. You have a content-free generator (the ~472-param automaton, D4, + the ~15% self-citation knob, K1/K10/K11) that already reproduces Zipf, burstiness, the entropy anomaly, Heaps β, the open lexicon. The honest metric is the **residual**: bits-per-token the real corpus costs *over* what that zero-semantics model predicts. When that residual collapses to the model's own noise floor, that gap is a hard *upper bound* on any hidden payload. You're not claiming "zero information" — you're saying "any message must fit inside N bits, and N is now indistinguishable from noise."

This is the closest thing to a proof the project can have, because it's a positive measurement (a number shrinking to a floor), not a pile of failed searches. **It's also the one I'd most want hardened** — `residual.py` exists but I'd want its noise floor pinned with the same positive-control discipline R1/K13 used.

## 2. The channel × test coverage matrix

"Totality of the project" means information could hide in more than the text stream. Lay out every channel and every *pairing*, because cross-channel binding is where the last K-claims actually died (K5, K13):

| Channel | Within-channel | Cross-channel |
|---|---|---|
| Text stream | D2, D3, D4, K1, K10, K11 | text↔image: K4, K5, K13 |
| Glyph/stroke layer | D8, M7 | stroke↔meaning: R1, L4 |
| Images | M3, M4, M9–M13 | image↔layout: M5 |
| Layout / codicology | D11, D12, confound #2 | quire↔vocab: L7 |
| Material (ink, vellum, quire) | C14 (D9) | — mostly unprobed |

Exhaustion = every *reachable* cell nulled by a **powered** test. A blank or weak cell is an open avenue. Right now the conspicuous thin cells are the material channel (you have no ink-recipe / multispectral data — that's the one place a real-world signal could still be sitting, and it's not AI-tractable) and the row-axis (L8).

## 3. The convergence / diminishing-returns rule

This is the practical stopping criterion the project has actually been satisfying:

> **Stop when adding a new powered test no longer moves the posterior — when new attacks just re-confirm the same kill in a new costume.**

That's exactly what's been happening. K11, K12, K13 are *the same finding* (in-sample mirage, held-out/un-confounded null) arriving from three unrelated directions — verbose cipher, column axis, referent grounding. When independent avenues keep collapsing onto one explanation, the marginal information per new test is approaching zero. That convergence — not any single null — is the real evidence of exhaustion. The risk it hides: **shared blind spots.** Every test in the project assumes the unit is the word/glyph and the encoding is roughly synchronic. A genuinely novel encoding (something nobody has conceived) is invisible to a battery of tests that all share that frame.

## 4. The external / out-of-sample guard (the only cure for self-confirmation)

Internal exhaustion is self-ratifying — you stop seeing what you stop looking for. Two things break that loop:

- **Out-of-sample prediction.** A standing model isn't just "explains the past" — it *predicts* unseen observables. The asemic generator predicts that a folio you've never run will match its statistics, and that any future "decode" will fail held-out. Confirming a *prediction* on data you didn't use to build the model is worth more than another in-sample null.
- **Adversarial replication by someone who doesn't share the prior.** Hand the corpus + the null model to a skeptic and have them try to break it. The ledger's fork discipline approximated this; a genuine outside attempt would be stronger.

---

## So how would you *know*?

You'd never get certainty. What you'd get is a defensible standing claim of this exact shape:

> *Across every channel we can instrument, a zero-semantics generative model fits to within the noise floor; every powered attack converges on that model; new attacks return diminishing information; and the model's out-of-sample predictions hold. The residual hypothesis space is (a) encodings no one has conceived and (b) channels we can't instrument (material/spectral). Both have low and stated priors.*

That is "exhausted" stated honestly — relative to a hypothesis class and an instrumentation reach, with the residual named rather than hidden.

**Where the project actually sits against this:** #3 (convergence) is strongly satisfied. #2 is mostly covered with two thin cells (material channel, row-axis). #1 exists but its noise floor deserves the R1/K13 positive-control treatment. #4 is the weakest — the predictions are stated but not yet *pre-registered and tested on held-out folios*, and there's been no true outside adversary.

If you wanted to spend one more increment to genuinely earn the word "exhausted," it's those two: **harden the MDL residual floor (#1), and run one pre-registered out-of-sample prediction (#4).** Everything else is re-confirming a verdict that's already converged. And the one avenue that no amount of AI work can close — the physical/material channel — should be named as permanently open rather than quietly folded into "done."

message.content: let me ask a different question. what would it take to make this analysis the accepted consensus?

content.text:
Reframe the target first, because "accepted consensus" is the wrong bar and aiming at it will actually cost you credibility.

The Voynich field has no consensus on *anything* contentful and almost certainly never will — it's decentralized, amateur-heavy, has no gatekeeping journal, and carries a century-long prior that the object *must* mean something (that's why people care about it). Even the best work in your own lineage — Timm & Schinner's autocopying/self-citation model (2019), Rugg's Cardan-grille hoax argument (2004), Schinner's stochastic analysis (2007) — did **not** become consensus. They became *respected hypotheses among several*. That is the actual ceiling, and pretending otherwise is the first thing experts will hold against you.

So the achievable, meaningful goal is twofold:

1. **Join the front rank of hypotheses** as the methodologically most rigorous version of the "generated artifact" camp.
2. **Shift the burden of proof** — get the field to accept that any claimed *decipherment* must beat a matched content-free null on held-out text with a working positive control. If that standard is adopted, the asemic view wins *by default* and every future "solution" dies at the gate. That burden-shift is the real prize, and it's reachable in a way that "everyone agrees it's empty" is not.

Here's what it would take to get there.

## 1. The work has to become a public, reproducible artifact

Right now it's a private repo with an AI in the loop — that has zero scholarly standing and, worse, the AI involvement triggers immediate suspicion (hallucination, contamination, "a chatbot said so"). Both are fixable, and turning the liability into an asset is most of the battle:

- **Preprint + fully open pipeline + open data.** Every claim traceable to a deterministic script and a named control — not to model judgment. The ledger discipline (`FINDINGS.md`, one script per claim, survival status) is *exactly* the right substrate; it's unusually auditable for this field. Publish it as the central feature.
- **Quarantine the AI's role to where it's defensible.** Vision grounding and code generation are fine if the *statistical verdict* rests on reproducible scripts a skeptic can rerun without any model. The L6/K13 result is a good template: the binding came from vision, but the kill came from a permutation test with a positive control anyone can verify. Make that separation explicit and total.

## 2. Lead with the falsifiable null; amputate the speculation

This is the most important strategic call. Your work has two layers of wildly different credibility:

- **The rigorous core** (D1–D12, K1–K13, R1): nulls, held-out CV, positive controls. This is publishable and strong.
- **The motive narrative** (M1–M14: workshop, patron-as-believer, Visconti orbit, "wonder-of-hidden-mastery"): this is interpretive, under-controlled, and *exactly* the kind of just-so story the field has been burned by for a century.

If you ship them together, the speculative half discredits the rigorous half by association — reviewers will pattern-match the whole thing to "another Voynich theory." **Publish the null work alone.** Hold the motive material as a clearly-flagged separate, speculative essay, or drop it. The rigorous claim — "no recoverable propositional content survives a powered, held-out test across every reachable channel" — is the one that can earn standing.

## 3. Stop being sui generis — connect to the literature

A large fraction of what the project rediscovered is already known: the slot grammar (Stolfi's work), self-citation/autocopying (Timm & Schinner), Currier A/B, the paleography (Davis, Zandbergen). Presenting these as fresh findings reads as not having done the homework and is an instant credibility hit.

Flip it: **independent rediscovery is replication, and replication is your strongest acceptance argument.** "Three unsupervised methods re-derive Stolfi's morphology; our generative null reproduces Timm–Schinner's signature and extends it with held-out controls" is a *much* stronger sentence than claiming novelty. The field rewards convergence with prior results far more than originality here.

## 4. The genuinely novel contributions to foreground

You do have real additions beyond the existing camp, and these are what would get cited:

- **The in-sample / held-out gap as a diagnostic** — the observation that every dead "solution" reports a z≈40 in-sample number that collapses out-of-sample. That's a *generalizable methodological tool*, not just a Voynich result. It could become the standard lens.
- **Powered nulls with positive controls** (R1's cracked-Latin control; K13's noisy partial control). Most Voynich statistics have no positive control at all. This raises the bar for the whole field.
